title: א־ב  The alphabet
hook: Hebrew reads right to left and has no capital letters. Vowels are usually not written — you fill them in from context (that's what the transliteration is for). Five letters take a special 'final' shape at the end of a word.

examples.hint: kaf, mem, nun, pe, tzadi — same letters, tail forms

title: ה־  the
hook: Hebrew has no separate word for "the". You attach a single ה (ha) to the front of the noun. There's no "a/an" at all — a bare noun is already "a ___".

examples.prompt: Now build it — the water (מים / mayim)

title: ו־  and
rule: glue ו (ve) onto the next word = "and"
hook: "And" is never its own word — it's a ו stuck to the front of what follows.

examples.prompt: bread and water (לחם / lechem · מים / mayim)
examples.hint: ve softens to "u" before some letters

examples.prompt: you and I (אתה / ata · אני / ani)

title: ב־  in / at
rule: glue ב (be) onto the front = "in / at"
hook: Location and "in" ride along on a ב attached to the noun.

title: ל־  to / for
rule: glue ל (le) onto the front = "to / for"
hook: Direction and "for" attach as a ל. It's also the mark of the infinitive: לבוא = "to come".

title: מ־  from
rule: glue מ (mi / me) onto the front = "from"
hook: "From" is a מ attached to the front — mi- before a plain noun, me- before the letter ה.

examples.prompt: the house → from the house (הבית / ha-bayit)

title: ש־  that / which / who
rule: glue ש (she) onto the front to link clauses
hook: One tiny ש does the work of English "that", "which", and "who" — it glues onto the start of the second clause.

examples.prompt: the man who came (איש / ish · בא / ba)

title: את  the object marker
rule: put את (et) before a definite object
hook: When the thing receiving the action is definite — "the book", "it", a name — Hebrew flags it with את (et). It has no English translation; it just points at the object. Indefinite objects get no את.

examples.answer: אני אוהב את זה  (ani ohev et ze)

examples.prompt: I see the boy (רואה / roe · הילד)
examples.answer: אני רואה את הילד  (ani roe et ha-yeled)

examples.prompt: I want water — indefinite, so NO et
